mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW X3 35i engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW X3 35i engine replacement typically costs between £1,800 and £6,200 for the engine itself, depending on condition (used, reconditioned or rebuilt). The N55B30 high-output turbo unit commands premium pricing due to specialist rebuild requirements. Used engine: £1,800-£3,500. Reconditioned: £2,800-£4,800. Rebuilt: £3,500-£6,200. Labour (supply & fit): £500-£900 for independent specialist.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of water pump failure in a BMW X3 35i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The N55's electric water pump can fail without warning. Common signs include overheating warnings, the radiator fan running at maximum speed, coolant loss, and the engine entering limp mode. Overheating warning or temperature gauge in the red. Radiator fan running at full speed constantly. Coolant loss with no visible external leak. If ignored: engine overheating and potential head gasket failure.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW X3 35i?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, replacing the engine on a BMW X3 35i is usually worthwhile given the vehicle's performance credentials and strong residual values. A typical 2010-2017 X3 35i is worth £5,000-£15,000 - replacement cost is often justified, particularly on well-maintained examples. X3 35i values remain strong for performance SUV buyers. Rebuilt engine costs significantly less than vehicle replacement. Supply and fit service minimises downtime. Engine replacement extends vehicle life by 80,000+ miles.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW X3 35i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW X3 35i engine replacement typically takes 2-4 days for a specialist to complete, including removal of the old unit, fitting the replacement engine, ECU coding, and full road testing. Typical labour time: 12-16 hours. Allow 2-4 working days for the full job. xDrive system calibration adds additional time.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW X3 35i and the X3 28i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 35i uses the 306hp N55B30 3.0-litre turbocharged straight-six, while the 28i uses either the N52B30 naturally aspirated straight-six (272hp) or the N20B20 turbo four-cylinder (245hp). The 35i is significantly faster and more responsive, with 400Nm of torque available from just 1,200rpm. 35i: 306hp, 3.0L turbo straight-six, 400Nm torque. 28i: 245-272hp, 2.0L turbo four or 3.0L naturally aspirated. 35i offers superior performance and the classic straight-six soundtrack.

The N55 is generally reliable, but common issues include electric water pump failure, valve cover gasket oil leaks, high-pressure fuel pump failure, and charge pipe cracking. Regular maintenance and preventative replacement of known weak points can extend engine life significantly. N55 is generally robust with proper maintenance. Electric water pump is the most common failure point. Oil leaks from valve cover and oil filter housing are common. Regular cooling system and fuel system inspections are essential.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW X3 35i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW X3 35i arrived with the F25 generation in 2010 as the performance-oriented petrol flagship, powered by the N55B30 3.0-litre turbocharged straight-six - BMW's first mass-produced single twin-scroll turbo engine. It delivered 306hp and 400Nm of torque, making the X3 35i the quickest petrol X3 of its generation.

milestones.description: N55B30, 3.0-litre twin-scroll turbo straight-six petrol, 306hp, launched in the F25 X3 xDrive35i
xDrive35i available across SE, Sport and M Sport trims
N55B30A updated variant with revised engine management
F25 LCI facelift; xDrive35i continues with N55B30A
G01 generation launches; xDrive35i replaced by X3 M40i with B58 engine
F25 production ends; the 35i badge is discontinued in the X3 range

commonProblems.h2: BMW X3 35i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW X3 35i's N55 straight-six is BMW's first mass-produced turbocharged petrol engine - responsive, powerful, and generally reliable. However, age and mileage bring well-documented issues with the cooling system, oil leaks, and high-pressure fuel system. Rebuilt BMW X3 35i engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: N55 Electric Water Pump Failure - Why X3 35i Engines Overheat Without Warning
problems.rootCause: The N55 uses an electric water pump that can fail without warning. Unlike belt-driven pumps, there is no gradual deterioration - failure is often sudden, leading to rapid overheating and potential head gasket failure. This is one of the most common N55 engine problems.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace water pump, thermostat, coolant flush
Supply & fit, new water pump, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If overheating has damaged the engine

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2010-2017 BMW X3 35i is worth approximately £5,000-£15,000. Replacement cost is usually justified on higher-value examples; for cars under £6,000, evaluate carefully. These are performance SUVs - engine replacement is often worthwhile if the body and transmission are sound.
problems.recommendation: On the N55, the electric water pump is a consumable item. Replace it preventatively at 60,000 miles or 8 years - a £450-£800 specialist job is cheap insurance against a £3,500+ engine replacement. Watch for warning signs: overheating warnings, limp mode, or the radiator fan running at maximum speed.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt N55B30 BMW X3 35i engine prices

problems.h4: N55 Oil Leaks - Valve Cover and Oil Filter Housing Gasket Failure
problems.rootCause: The N55's plastic valve cover becomes brittle from engine heat, causing gasket failure and oil leaks onto the exhaust manifold. The oil filter housing gasket is also a common leak point. Oil leaks can lead to low oil pressure and, if ignored, engine damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace valve cover gasket and breather hoses
Replace gasket, new oil and filter
repairOptions.longevity: Essential if leaking - prevents oil starvation
If oil leaks have caused low oil pressure damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2010-2017 BMW X3 35i is worth approximately £5,000-£15,000. Gasket replacements are cost-effective - engine replacement is only justified if the engine has suffered catastrophic damage.
problems.recommendation: Oil leaks on the N55 are almost inevitable with age. A £350-£600 valve cover gasket replacement at a specialist is far cheaper than waiting for oil to damage the wiring or for low oil pressure to destroy the engine. If you smell burning oil or see smoke from the engine bay, have the gaskets inspected immediately.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt N55B30 BMW X3 35i engine prices

problems.h4: N55 HPFP & Injector Failure - Fuel System Problems
problems.rootCause: The high-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) can fail, causing hard starts, long cranking, and loss of power. Injector failures are also common, particularly on cylinder 5, leading to rough idling and misfires.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace failed injector(s), code to ECU
repairOptions.longevity: If one fails, consider replacing all six

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, new fuel system components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If fuel system failure has caused engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2010-2017 BMW X3 35i is worth approximately £5,000-£15,000. Fuel system repairs are usually cost-effective - engine replacement is only required if the HPFP has failed catastrophically.
problems.recommendation: If your X3 35i has long cranking times, hard starts, or misfires under load, have the fuel system inspected. HPFP failure is well-documented on the N55. A £550-£950 specialist repair is far cheaper than a full engine replacement. If one injector fails beyond 80,000 miles, consider replacing all six to avoid repeated garage visits.

problems.h4: N55 Turbocharger & Charge Pipe Issues - Loss of Boost
problems.rootCause: The N55's turbocharger wastegate can develop rattle or fail to close properly. The plastic charge pipe can crack under boost pressure, causing loss of power and boost leaks.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace with upgraded aluminium charge pipe
Replace wastegate actuator or turbo unit
Supply & fit, new turbo components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If turbo failure has sent debris into the engine

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2010-2017 BMW X3 35i is worth approximately £5,000-£15,000. Charge pipe and turbo repairs are usually cost-effective; engine replacement is only required if turbo failure has caused engine damage.
problems.recommendation: The plastic charge pipe is a known weak point - upgrade to an aluminium replacement preventatively. If you hear a rattling noise from the turbo area or experience loss of boost, have the wastegate inspected. A £250-£450 charge pipe upgrade is excellent value on a performance SUV.
